pure-announcement.rationale: This is a peer-reviewable arXiv security-measurement paper with a named methodology and framework, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: remote-first-mcp-governance prescribes an enterprise fix, mcp-oauth-discovery-ssrf and mcp-attack-surface-taxonomy name mechanisms and categories, but none of them is the empirical prevalence finding this paper contributes — an internet-scale measured baseline of how internet-facing MCP servers actually stand today.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Backed by a stated methodology (passive discovery across eleven data sources plus active dynamic testing via an open-sourced framework, 34 test modules over 10 vulnerability classes, four measurement runs) that is independently reproducible.

durability.rationale: The claim is structural, not a stat that ages out: internet-facing MCP servers are exposed by design because deployment velocity currently outpaces security review, evidenced by an open-sourced, reusable scanning methodology rather than a one-off vendor count.

actionability.rationale: It substantiates urgency and names the failure modes empirically (auth absence, unrestricted shell tools, days-long deployment churn) but does not hand the reader a new mitigation technique beyond the obvious 'turn on auth, restrict tools' already covered elsewhere.

atomicity.rationale: One coherent idea — internet-facing MCP servers are measurably exposed by design, evidenced by a purpose-built dynamic-scanning methodology across a real-world sample — stateable in one paragraph.
